
# How to Use Facebook: Complete Beginner's Guide


## What is this in plain English?


Think of Facebook like a giant community bulletin board from the 1970s, but instead of being in one location like a grocery store or library, it's accessible from anywhere in the world. Just as you might post a notice about a garage sale, read announcements from neighbors, or see photos from the local school play, Facebook lets you share updates, see what friends and family are doing, and stay connected—all from your phone or computer.


Facebook is like having a photo album, address book, newspaper, and party invitation system all in one place. You can share pictures of your grandchildren, see what old friends are up to, join groups about your hobbies, and keep in touch with people who live far away. It's a way to stay connected without making dozens of phone calls or mailing letters.


The key difference from real bulletin boards? On Facebook, you control who sees your posts (like choosing which neighbors to invite into your home), and you can see updates from friends instantly (like getting a letter the moment it's written instead of waiting for mail delivery).


## Before You Start: What You Need to Know About Facebook


**What Facebook is good for:**

- Staying connected with family and friends, especially those who live far away
- Seeing photos of grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and relatives
- Keeping up with old friends from high school, college, or former workplaces
- Sharing your own photos and updates about your life
- Joining groups about hobbies, interests, or your local community
- Finding and RSVPing to events like reunions, parties, or community gatherings
- Following organizations, businesses, or public figures you care about

**What Facebook is NOT:**

- A replacement for phone calls or in-person visits (it's a supplement, not a substitute)
- Completely private (anything you post can potentially be seen by more people than you intend)
- Required for a happy life (plenty of people don't use it and that's perfectly fine)
- Something you need to understand completely to enjoy (you can use just the basic features)

**What you'll need:**

- A computer, tablet, or smartphone with internet access
- An email address (if you don't have one, we can help you get one)
- About 45-60 minutes to set up your account and learn the basics
- Patience with yourself as you learn—everyone starts as a beginner
- No prior social media experience needed

**Important to understand from the start:**

- Facebook is free because they make money from advertisements (you'll see ads mixed in with posts)
- Privacy matters—we'll teach you how to control who sees what you share
- Not everything you see on Facebook is true—we'll help you spot misinformation
- You don't need to use every feature—stick with what makes sense to you
> **For Complete Beginners:** Don't feel overwhelmed. You're not expected to understand everything immediately. This guide will take you step by step, and you can always come back and reread sections. There's no test at the end, and you can't break anything by exploring. Take your time and learn at your own pace.

## Step 1: Creating Your Facebook Account


Let's start from the very beginning and create your Facebook account. If you already have one, skip to Step 2.


**What You'll Need Before Starting:**

1. **An email address** - This is how Facebook will contact you and how you'll log in
    - If you don't have email: Ask a family member to help you set up a Gmail, Yahoo, or Outlook account first
    - Write down your email address and password on paper to keep safely
2. **A way to access the internet:**
    - Computer: Any laptop or desktop with an internet browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge)
    - Tablet: iPad, Android tablet, or similar device
    - Smartphone: iPhone or Android phone

**Creating Your Account on a Computer:**

1. **Open your internet browser**
    - Look for icons like: Chrome (colorful circle), Safari (blue compass), Firefox (orange fox), or Edge (blue wave)
    - Click to open it
2. **Type in the address bar at the top:**
    - `www.facebook.com`
    - Press Enter on your keyboard
3. **You'll see the Facebook homepage with a sign-up form**
    - On the right side, you'll see boxes to fill in
4. **Fill in the sign-up form:First name:** Your actual first name (e.g., "Mary")
**Last name:** Your actual last name (e.g., "Johnson")
**Email:** Type your email address
**Re-enter email:** Type it again to confirm
**Password:** Create a password for Facebook
**Birthday:** Select your birth month, day, and year
**Gender:** Select male, female, or custom
    - Don't use nicknames here—use your real name so friends can find you
    - This helps old friends recognize you
    - Example: [maryjohnson@gmail.com](mailto:maryjohnson@gmail.com)
    - Type carefully—one wrong letter means you won't receive Facebook's messages
    - This makes sure you didn't make a typo
    - At least 6 characters (but longer is better)
    - Mix of letters, numbers, and symbols
    - Example: MyGarden2024!
    - **Write this down on paper and keep it safe**
    - Don't use the same password as your email
    - Facebook uses this to verify you're old enough (must be 13+)
    - You can hide your birth year from others later
5. **Click the green "Sign Up" button**
6. **Confirm your email address:**
    - Facebook will send a confirmation code to your email
    - Open your email (in a different window or tab)
    - Find the email from Facebook (check spam folder if you don't see it)
    - The email will have a 5 or 6-digit number
    - Type that number into Facebook
    - Click "Confirm"

**Congratulations! You now have a Facebook account.**


**Creating Your Account on a Smartphone or Tablet:**

1. **Find and open your app store:**
    - iPhone/iPad: App Store (blue icon with white "A")
    - Android: Play Store (colorful triangle)
2. **Search for "Facebook"**
    - Tap the search icon (magnifying glass)
    - Type: Facebook
    - Tap Search
3. **Download the official Facebook app:**
    - Look for the app with blue background and white "f"
    - Made by "Meta Platforms, Inc."
    - Tap "Get" (iPhone) or "Install" (Android)
    - Wait for it to download (may take 1-2 minutes)
4. **Open the Facebook app:**
    - Tap "Open" after it downloads
    - Or find the blue Facebook icon on your home screen
5. **Create your account:**
    - Tap "Create New Account"
    - Follow the same steps as above (entering name, email, password, birthday, gender)
    - Confirm your email when prompted

**After Creating Your Account:**


Facebook will immediately ask you to do several things. Let's skip most of these for now and do them properly later:


**Skip these for now (click "Skip" or "Not Now"):**

- ❌ "Find friends" - We'll do this carefully later
- ❌ "Add profile picture" - We'll add a good one later
- ❌ "Complete your profile" - We'll do this with privacy in mind
- ❌ "Follow pages" - You can explore these later

**Why skip these?** Because we want to set up your privacy settings FIRST before adding friends or information. This ensures everything you share is as private as you want it to be from the beginning.

> **Troubleshooting Common Issues:**
> - **"Email already in use":** You or someone else may have already created an account with that email. Try clicking "Forgot Password" to recover it.
> - **"Invalid email":** Check for typos. Make sure you typed .com (not .con or .cm)
> - **"Password too weak":** Add numbers or symbols to make it stronger
> - **"Can't verify email":** Check spam/junk folder for the confirmation code
>

## Step 2: Understanding the Facebook Homepage (News Feed)


Now that you have an account, let's learn what you're looking at when you open Facebook.


**Accessing Facebook:**


**On a computer:**

- Open your browser
- Type: [www.facebook.com](http://www.facebook.com/)
- Press Enter
- You should be automatically logged in
- If not, enter your email and password, then click "Log In"

**On a smartphone/tablet:**

- Tap the blue Facebook icon
- It should open to your main page
- If not, enter your email and password

**What You're Looking At - The Main Screen:**


When you first open Facebook, you're looking at what's called your **News Feed** or **Home**. Think of this as the main bulletin board where you see updates from everyone.


**At the very top of the screen (The Blue Bar):**


This blue bar stays at the top no matter where you go on Facebook. Here's what each icon means:


**Left side:**

- **"f" logo** (or "Facebook" text): Click this to return to your News Feed from anywhere on Facebook
- **Search bar**: A magnifying glass icon where you can search for friends, pages, or groups

**Right side (on computer):**

- **Your name and small picture**: Click this to see your own profile
- **Home icon** (little house): Your News Feed
- **Friends icon** (two people): See friend requests and find friends
- **Messenger icon** (speech bubble with lightning bolt): Private messages
- **Notifications icon** (bell): Alerts about activity on your posts
- **Menu** (9 dots or three lines): More options and settings

**On smartphone, the icons are at the bottom instead:**

- **Home** (house)
- **Watch** (TV icon) - videos
- **Marketplace** (storefront) - local buying/selling
- **Groups** (people in circle)
- **Menu** (three lines) - settings and more

**The Main Area - Your News Feed:**


This is the large center area where you'll see posts from friends. It's like a constantly updating newspaper made up of what your friends share.


**What you'll see in the News Feed:**

1. **"What's on your mind?"** box at the top
    - This is where you'll create your own posts
    - We'll cover this in detail later
2. **Stories** (circular profile pictures in a row)
    - These are photos/videos that disappear after 24 hours
    - You can click to view them, but we'll skip these for now
3. **Posts from friends and pages:**
    - These appear as individual boxes stacked vertically
    - Scroll down to see more posts
    - New posts appear at the top

**What a typical post looks like:**


`[Profile Picture] Friend's Name
2 hours ago · 📍 Location

Here's the text of their post! Maybe they're sharing 
what they did today or a thought they had.

[Photo or video might appear here]

👍 Like    💬 Comment    ↗️ Share

10 people like this
View 3 comments`


**Understanding the post elements:**

- **Profile Picture and Name**: Who posted it
- **Time stamp**: When they posted it ("2 hours ago", "Yesterday", "March 15")
- **Location tag** (optional): Where they were when posting
- **Text**: What they wrote
- **Photo/Video** (optional): Visual content they shared
- **Reactions**: The number of people who liked or reacted
- **Like button**: Click to show you liked the post (thumb icon)
- **Comment button**: Click to write a response
- **Share button**: Click to repost it to your own friends

**The Left Sidebar (on computer):**


This area shows shortcuts and links:

- Your profile
- Friends list
- Groups you've joined
- Pages you follow
- Saved posts
- Marketplace
- Memories (old posts from years ago)

**The Right Sidebar (on computer):**


This shows:

- Friend requests (people who want to be your friend)
- Upcoming birthdays of friends
- Sponsored ads (advertisements)
- Suggested friends or pages
> **Don't Feel Overwhelmed:** You don't need to understand or use everything right away. Most people primarily use just the News Feed to see what friends post and occasionally post their own updates. The rest is extra features you can explore when ready.

## Step 3: Setting Up Your Privacy Settings (VERY IMPORTANT)


Before you do anything else on Facebook—before adding friends, posting, or adding photos—let's make sure your account is private and secure. This is crucial.


**Why Privacy Matters:**


Without proper settings:

- Strangers can see your personal information
- Your posts might be visible to the entire internet
- Scammers can gather information about you
- You have less control over your Facebook experience

With good privacy:

- Only friends you approve can see your posts
- Personal information stays private
- You control who can contact you
- You're safer from scams

**Accessing Privacy Settings:**


**On a computer:**

1. Click the **down arrow** in the top-right corner of the blue bar
2. Click **Settings & Privacy**
3. Click **Settings**
4. Click **Privacy** in the left sidebar

**On a smartphone:**

1. Tap the **three horizontal lines** (menu icon) in the bottom-right (iPhone) or top-right (Android)
2. Scroll down and tap **Settings & Privacy**
3. Tap **Settings**
4. Tap **Privacy**

**The Most Important Privacy Settings:**


**Setting #1: Who can see your future posts?**


This controls who sees everything you post from now on.

1. Look for **"Who can see your future posts?"**
2. Click or tap on it
3. You'll see these options:
    - **Public** - Anyone on or off Facebook (NOT recommended)
    - **Friends** - Only your Facebook friends (RECOMMENDED)
    - **Friends except...** - Friends minus certain people
    - **Specific friends** - Only certain friends you choose
    - **Only me** - Just you (good for drafts)
4. **Select "Friends"** - This is the safest option for most people
5. Click **Close**

**What this means:** From now on, when you post something, only people you've accepted as friends will see it. Strangers scrolling Facebook won't see your posts.


**Setting #2: Who can send you friend requests?**

1. Find **"Who can send you friend requests?"**
2. Click or tap it
3. Options:
    - **Everyone** - Any Facebook user (not recommended)
    - **Friends of friends** - People who know someone you know (RECOMMENDED)
4. Select **"Friends of friends"**

**What this means:** Random strangers who have no connection to you can't send friend requests. Only people who have mutual friends with you can.


**Setting #3: Who can look you up using your email address?**

1. Find **"Who can look you up using the email address you provided?"**
2. Click or tap it
3. Select **"Friends"** or **"Friends of friends"**

Do the same for:

- **"Who can look you up using the phone number you provided?"**
- Select **"Friends"** or **"Friends of friends"**

**What this means:** People can't find your profile by typing in your email or phone number unless they're already connected to you.


**Setting #4: Do you want search engines to link to your profile?**

1. Find **"Do you want search engines outside of Facebook to link to your profile?"**
2. If it says "Yes" or the toggle is ON (blue), click to turn it OFF (gray)

**What this means:** Your Facebook profile won't show up when people Google your name.


**Setting Up Your Profile Privacy:**


Now let's control what information people can see about you.

1. Go back to Settings (click the back arrow or **Settings** in the menu)
2. Click or tap your **name** at the top, or click **Profile**
3. Click **About** below your name
4. You'll see sections like Contact Info, Basic Info, Work, etc.

**For each section:**

1. Click the **Edit** button or the section name
2. Next to each piece of information, you'll see a privacy icon (looks like two people or a globe)
3. Click that icon
4. Change it to **"Friends"** or **"Only me"**

**Key information to keep private:**

- **Phone number** - Set to "Only me" (strangers don't need this)
- **Email** - Set to "Friends" or "Only me"
- **Birthday** - Show month and day to friends, but hide the year
- **Home address** - DELETE this entirely or set to "Only me"
- **Work history** - Set to "Friends"
- **Education** - Set to "Friends"

**After adjusting privacy settings:**

1. Click **"View As"** on your profile (or **three dots** > **View As**)
2. Select **"View as Public"**
3. This shows you what strangers see
4. You should see very little information
5. If you see too much, go back and adjust those settings
> **Critical Safety Note:** These settings are your first line of defense against scams, identity theft, and unwanted contact. Don't skip this step. It only takes 10 minutes and protects you for as long as you use Facebook.

## Step 4: Adding a Profile Picture and Cover Photo


Now that your privacy is set, let's personalize your profile so friends can recognize you.


**What are Profile Pictures and Cover Photos?**

- **Profile Picture**: Small circular photo that appears next to your name everywhere on Facebook
    - Think of it like a photo ID badge
    - Appears next to every post you make
    - Should be a clear photo of your face
    - Always visible to everyone (even non-friends can see this)
- **Cover Photo**: Large rectangular photo at the top of your profile
    - Like a banner or billboard
    - Shows your personality or interests
    - Can be more creative than profile picture
    - Visibility depends on your settings

**Adding Your Profile Picture:**


**On a computer:**

1. Click your **name** in the top-right corner (or click **Profile** in the menu)
2. You'll see a gray silhouette where your profile picture should be
3. **Hover** your mouse over it
4. Click **"Add Profile Picture"** or the **camera icon**
5. Choose one of these options:
    - **Upload Photo**: Select a photo from your computer
    - **Take Photo**: Use your computer's webcam (if it has one)
6. Navigate to where your photos are stored (Pictures folder, Desktop, etc.)
7. Click the photo you want
8. Click **"Open"**
9. You'll see a preview with a crop box—you can drag to reposition your face in the circle
10. Click **"Save"**

**On a smartphone:**

1. Tap your **profile icon** or **name**
2. Tap the gray silhouette or camera icon where your picture should be
3. Choose:
    - **Take Photo**: Open your camera to take a selfie
    - **Choose from Library**: Pick an existing photo
4. Select your photo
5. Use your fingers to zoom and position your face in the circle
6. Tap **"Save"** or **"Done"**

**Tips for a Good Profile Picture:**


**Good profile pictures:**

- ✓ Clear photo of your face
- ✓ Good lighting (not too dark)
- ✓ You're smiling or looking friendly
- ✓ Recent photo (helps friends recognize you now)
- ✓ Just you (not a group photo)
- ✓ Professional or casual—whatever represents you

**Avoid:**

- ✗ Blurry or dark photos
- ✗ Photos where you're very far away
- ✗ Group photos (people won't know which person is you)
- ✗ Sunglasses covering your face
- ✗ Photos of pets, cars, or objects (use a photo of YOU)

**Adding a Cover Photo:**

1. On your profile, look at the large rectangle at the top
2. Click or tap **"Add Cover Photo"**
3. Choose **"Upload Photo"**
4. Select a photo
5. The preview lets you drag the photo up/down to position it
6. Click **"Save"**

**Cover Photo Ideas:**

- Beautiful landscape or nature photo
- Photo from a favorite vacation
- Photo with family members
- Your garden or hobby
- A meaningful place
- Keep it appropriate (anyone can see this)

**Changing Your Photos Later:**


You can change these anytime:

1. Go to your profile
2. **Hover over** (computer) or **tap** (phone) your profile picture or cover photo
3. Click **"Update"** or the **camera icon**
4. Choose **"Upload New Photo"**
5. Select a different photo
6. Save

**Privacy Note About Profile Pictures:**


Profile pictures are ALWAYS public (visible to everyone, even people not on Facebook). This is how Facebook works—it helps people find and recognize you.


**If you're concerned about privacy:**

- Use a photo that shows your face but not your home/location
- Don't include sensitive information in the background
- You can still be on Facebook without a profile picture (though friends may not recognize you)
> **Don't Worry About Perfect Photos:** Your profile picture doesn't need to be professional or perfect. A simple, clear photo of you smiling is perfect. Friends just want to recognize you. You can always change it later if you find a photo you like better.

## Step 5: Finding and Adding Friends


Now that your profile is set up, let's connect with people you know. Finding friends is what makes Facebook useful—without friends, you're just looking at an empty page!


**Understanding Facebook Friendship:**


On Facebook, "friends" means:

- People you've connected with on the platform
- They can see your posts (if set to Friends), and you can see theirs
- You must both agree to be friends (one person sends a request, the other accepts)
- You can have up to 5,000 friends (but most people have 50-300)
- Quality over quantity—it's better to have 20 real friends than 500 strangers

**How to Find People You Know:**


**Method 1: Search by Name**

1. Look at the **search bar** at the top of Facebook (has a magnifying glass icon)
2. Click or tap in the search bar
3. Type a person's name
    - Example: "John Smith"
4. Press **Enter** or click the **Search icon**
5. You'll see search results showing people with that name
6. Look for the right person by checking:
    - Their profile picture
    - Where they live or work (if shown)
    - Mutual friends (friends you have in common)
7. Click or tap on their name to view their profile
8. If it's the right person, click **"Add Friend"**

**Tips for searching:**

- Try different name variations (Robert vs. Bob, Elizabeth vs. Beth)
- Add their city or workplace to narrow results: "John Smith Chicago"
- Look for mutual friends to verify you found the right person

**Method 2: Import Contacts (Optional)**


Facebook can look at your email contacts to find people you know.


**On computer:**

1. Click the **Friends icon** (two people) in the top-right
2. Click **"Find Friends"**
3. Click **"Add Personal Contacts"** (or similar option)
4. Choose your email provider (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook, etc.)
5. Log into your email (Facebook will look at your contacts)
6. Facebook shows you which contacts have Facebook accounts
7. Click **"Add Friend"** next to people you want to connect with

**On smartphone:**

1. Tap the **Menu** (three lines)
2. Tap **"Friends"**
3. Tap **"Find Friends"** or **"Suggestions"**
4. Tap **"Upload contacts"** (may need to grant permission)

**Privacy note:** This shares your contact list with Facebook. If you're uncomfortable with this, use Method 1 (search by name) instead.


**Method 3: Friend Suggestions**


Facebook automatically suggests people you might know based on:

- Mutual friends (friends you have in common)
- Same hometown or school
- Same workplace
- Contact information

**To see suggestions:**

1. Click the **Friends icon** at the top (or tap **Menu** > **Friends** on phone)
2. Click **"Friend Requests"** then **"Suggestions"**
3. Scroll through suggested people
4. Click **"Add Friend"** if you recognize someone

**Method 4: Mutual Friends**


Once you have a few friends, you can find more through them:

1. Go to a friend's profile (click their name)
2. Click **"Friends"** below their name
3. You'll see their friends list
4. Look for people you recognize
5. Click their name to view their profile
6. Click **"Add Friend"**

**Sending a Friend Request:**


When you click "Add Friend":

- Facebook sends them a notification
- They can accept, decline, or ignore your request
- If they accept, you become friends
- If they decline or ignore, you won't be notified (you just won't become friends)
- You can't send another request to someone who declined

**Accepting Friend Requests:**


When someone wants to be your friend:

1. You'll see a notification (red number) on the **Friends icon**
2. Click or tap the Friends icon
3. You'll see friend requests with the person's name and picture
4. **Before accepting**, look at their profile:
    - Do you recognize them?
    - Do you have mutual friends?
    - Does their profile look real (has posts, photos, multiple friends)?
5. If you know them: Click **"Confirm"** or **"Accept"**
6. If you don't know them: Click **"Delete"** or **"Ignore"**

**Red Flags—DO NOT Accept These Friend Requests:**


❌ Someone with the same name as an existing friend (might be a fake account)
❌ Very attractive profile picture but only 20 friends and no posts (likely a scammer)
❌ Someone you don't know with no mutual friends
❌ Profile was just created (this week or month)
❌ Profile has only one photo and no personal posts
❌ Someone you blocked or removed as a friend before


**How Many Friends Should You Add?**


**For beginners, start small:**

- Week 1: Add 5-10 close friends and family
- Week 2-3: Add more friends as you get comfortable
- Month 2-3: Continue adding people you recognize and trust

**Don't feel pressure to:**

- Add people just to have more friends
- Accept requests from people you don't know
- Keep up with others who have hundreds of friends

**Managing Your Friends:**


**To see your friends list:**

1. Go to your profile
2. Click **"Friends"**
3. You'll see all your friends

**To unfriend someone:**

1. Go to their profile
2. Click **"Friends"** (checkmark button)
3. Click **"Unfriend"**
4. They won't be notified

**Why you might unfriend someone:**

- You no longer know them well
- They post content that makes you uncomfortable
- You realized you accepted a fake account
- Personal reasons

It's perfectly fine to keep your friends list small and curated.

> **Important Principle:** Only add people you actually know in real life. Facebook is for staying connected with existing relationships, not making friends with strangers. Your feed will be much more meaningful if it's full of people you genuinely care about.

## Step 6: Creating Your First Post


Now that you have some friends, it's time to share something! This is how you communicate with everyone on Facebook.


**What is a Post?**


A post is anything you share on Facebook:

- A text update about what you're doing or thinking
- A photo or video
- A link to an article or website
- Or a combination of these

When you post, it appears:

- In your friends' News Feeds (so they see it when scrolling)
- On your own profile (your timeline)

**Creating a Simple Text Post:**


**On a computer:**

1. Look at the top of your News Feed (home page)
2. Find the box that says **"What's on your mind?"**
3. Click inside the box
4. A larger window opens
5. Type what you want to share
    - Example: "Beautiful day today! Enjoying the sunshine in my garden."
    - Or: "Just finished reading a wonderful book."
6. Before posting, check the privacy setting:
    - Look for the icon next to your name (shows who can see this)
    - Should say **"Friends"** if you followed the privacy steps earlier
    - If it says **"Public"**, click it and change to **"Friends"**
7. Click the blue **"Post"** button

**Congratulations! You just created your first Facebook post!**


**On a smartphone:**

1. At the top of your News Feed, tap **"What's on your mind?"**
2. A new screen opens
3. Type your message in the text box
4. Check privacy setting (should say **"Friends"**)
5. Tap **"Post"** in the top-right corner

**What to Post About:**


**Good first posts:**

- "Hello Facebook! Excited to reconnect with friends."
- "Beautiful weather today! Hope everyone is doing well."
- "Just joined Facebook—looking forward to seeing what everyone is up to!"
- A simple update about your day or a thought you had

**Other ideas:**

- Share good news (graduations, achievements, celebrations)
- Comment on the weather or seasons
- Share a hobby or interest
- Ask friends a question
- Express gratitude or appreciation
- Share a memory or story

**What NOT to post:**

- Your full address or phone number (privacy risk)
- Complaints about people (can hurt feelings or relationships)
- Passwords or sensitive financial information
- Anything you wouldn't want an employer or grandchild to see
- Political rants that might alienate friends (unless your friends enjoy those discussions)
- Private medical information
- "I'm away on vacation for two weeks!" (tells burglars your home is empty)

**Adding a Photo to Your Post:**


**On a computer:**

1. Click in the **"What's on your mind?"** box
2. In the bottom of the post window, you'll see icons
3. Click the **Photo/Video** icon (looks like a picture)
4. Click **"Upload Photos/Video"**
5. Navigate to where your photos are stored
6. Click on a photo
7. Click **"Open"**
8. The photo appears in your post box
9. You can type a caption above the photo (optional)
10. Check privacy (Friends)
11. Click **"Post"**

**On a smartphone:**

1. Tap **"What's on your mind?"**
2. Tap the **Photo** icon at the bottom
3. Choose a photo from your camera roll
4. Tap **"Done"** or **"Next"**
5. Add text if desired
6. Tap **"Post"**

**Tips for Good Facebook Posts:**


**Length:**

- Short is fine (one sentence)
- A few sentences is good
- Very long posts (multiple paragraphs) might lose people's attention

**Tone:**

- Friendly and positive generally gets the most engagement
- It's okay to share challenges, but constant negativity can be draining
- Think about how you'd want to hear about this in person

**Frequency:**

- You don't need to post every day
- Once or twice a week is plenty for most people
- Some people post several times a day, others once a month—both are fine

**Authenticity:**

- Be yourself
- Don't feel pressure to make your life look perfect
- People appreciate genuine posts more than showy ones

**Editing or Deleting a Post:**


Made a typo? Want to remove something you posted?


**To edit:**

1. Find your post
2. Click the **three dots** in the top-right corner of the post
3. Click **"Edit post"**
4. Make your changes
5. Click **"Save"**

**To delete:**

1. Find your post
2. Click the **three dots**
3. Click **"Move to trash"** or **"Delete"**
4. Confirm deletion
5. The post disappears (note: it can take up to 90 days for Facebook to fully remove it from their servers)

**Understanding Who Saw Your Post:**


After posting, you can see:

- **How many people liked it** (thumbs up icon)
- **How many people commented** (speech bubble icon)
- **How many people shared it** (arrow icon)

These numbers appear below your post. Click on them to see specifically who interacted.

> **Post with Confidence:** Your first post might feel awkward, but that's normal. Think of it like speaking up at a gathering of friends—you're just sharing a thought or update with people who care about you. Start simple, and you'll get more comfortable over time.

## Step 7: Interacting with Friends' Posts (Liking, Commenting, Sharing)


Facebook is a conversation, not a one-way street. Let's learn how to respond to what your friends share.


**The Three Main Ways to Interact:**

1. **Like** - Quick way to show you saw and appreciated the post
2. **Comment** - Write a response or conversation
3. **Share** - Repost it to your own friends

**How to Like a Post:**


This is the simplest and most common interaction.


**On a computer:**

1. Find a post from a friend in your News Feed
2. Below the post, you'll see a **thumbs up icon** with the word "Like"
3. Click "Like"
4. The icon turns blue (showing you liked it)
5. Your friend gets a notification that you liked their post

**On a smartphone:**

1. Find a post
2. Tap the **thumbs up icon** below the post
3. It turns blue

**What liking means:**

- "I saw this and I appreciate it"
- "I'm thinking of you"
- "I agree" or "I enjoyed this"
- It's a quick, low-effort way to stay connected

**You should like posts when:**

- Friend shares good news
- They post a photo you enjoy
- They say something you agree with or find interesting
- You want to show support

**Reactions (Beyond Just "Like"):**


Facebook offers more emotions than just a thumbs up.


**How to use reactions:**


**On a computer:**

1. Hover your mouse over the "Like" button (don't click)
2. Six emoji faces appear: Like 👍, Love ❤️, Care 🤗, Haha 😂, Wow 😮, Sad 😢, Angry 😠
3. Click the one that matches your feeling
4. It appears on the post

**On a smartphone:**

1. Press and hold the Like button
2. The six reactions appear
3. Tap the one you want

**When to use each:**

- **Like** 👍 - General approval, agreement, or acknowledgment
- **Love** ❤️ - Something touching, beautiful, or you really care about
- **Care** 🤗 - Showing support during difficult times
- **Haha** 😂 - Something funny or amusing
- **Wow** 😮 - Surprising, impressive, or amazing news
- **Sad** 😢 - Sympathy for difficult news
- **Angry** 😠 - Used sparingly—maybe for injustice or frustrating situations

**How to Comment on a Post:**


Comments are like having a conversation. Use these to respond with more than just an emoji.


**On a computer:**

1. Below the post, click **"Comment"**
2. A text box appears
3. Type your response
    - Example: "Congratulations! So happy for you!"
    - Or: "Beautiful photo! Where was this taken?"
4. Press **Enter** on your keyboard (or click "Post")
5. Your comment appears below the post

**On a smartphone:**

1. Tap **"Comment"** below the post
2. The keyboard appears
3. Type your comment
4. Tap **"Post"** or the **send icon** (arrow or paper airplane)

**Comment Ideas:**


**Good comments:**

- Congratulations or encouragement
- Answer questions they asked
- Share a related memory or story
- Compliment photos
- Ask follow-up questions
- Express sympathy or support

**Examples:**

- "Love this! Thanks for sharing."
- "Congratulations on the new grandchild!"
- "Beautiful garden! What kind of flowers are those?"
- "I remember when we did that together—such great memories!"
- "Thinking of you during this difficult time."

**Comment etiquette:**

- Be kind and positive
- Keep it relatively short (a few sentences)
- Don't write a novel (save long messages for private messages)
- Avoid controversial topics in public comments
- Don't correct minor typos or grammar (unless they asked)
- If you disagree, be respectful or skip commenting

**Viewing and Replying to Comments on Your Own Posts:**


When friends comment on your posts:

1. You'll see a notification (red number on the bell icon)
2. Click the **notification icon**
3. It shows who commented
4. Click on the notification to see the comment
5. To reply to their comment:
    - Click **"Reply"** below their comment
    - Type your response
    - Example: "Thank you so much!"
    - Press Enter

**How to Share a Post:**


Sharing means reposting something to your own friends (like forwarding an email).


**When to share:**

- Something funny, informative, or interesting you want others to see
- A cause or organization you support
- An article or video you found valuable
- A memory or post from years ago that you want to highlight again

**How to share:**


**On a computer:**

1. Click **"Share"** below the post
2. Choose:
    - **Share now (Friends)** - Immediately shares to your friends
    - **Share to News Feed** - Let's you add your own comment first (recommended)
    - **Share to a friend's timeline** - Posts it to a specific friend
    - **Share in a group** - If you're in groups
3. If you chose "Share to News Feed":
    - Add your own text above the shared post (optional but nice)
    - Example: "This made me laugh!" or "Great recipe!"
    - Check privacy setting
    - Click **"Post"**

**On a smartphone:**

1. Tap **"Share"**
2. Choose **"Share now"** or **"Write something about this"**
3. Add your comment
4. Tap **"Post"**

**Share thoughtfully:**

- Make sure the content is accurate before sharing (especially news)
- Don't share chain letters ("Share this or something bad will happen!")
- Don't share "copy and paste this" posts
- Don't share private messages or posts
- Credit the original poster if it's not theirs

**Hiding or Reporting Posts:**


If you see something you don't like in your feed:

1. Click the **three dots** in the top-right corner of the post
2. Options:
    - **"Hide post"** - You won't see it, but it's still on Facebook
    - **"Snooze [Friend Name] for 30 days"** - You won't see their posts for a month (useful if someone posts too much)
    - **"Unfollow [Friend Name]"** - Stay friends but don't see their posts (you can always re-follow later)
    - **"Report post"** - If it's spam, harassment, or violates Facebook's rules
> **Engagement Makes Facebook Better:** The more you like, comment, and share, the more Facebook shows you similar content. If you engage with friends' family photos, you'll see more of those. If you engage with news articles, you'll see more news. Your interactions shape your experience.

## Step 8: Understanding Your Profile and Timeline


Your profile is your personal space on Facebook—think of it as your house where visitors can see what you've shared. Let's explore it.


**Accessing Your Profile:**


**On a computer:**

- Click your **name** or **profile picture** in the top-right corner of the blue bar
- Or click **"Profile"** in the left menu

**On a smartphone:**

- Tap the **menu icon** (three horizontal lines)
- Tap your **name** at the top
- Or tap your **profile picture** wherever it appears

**What's On Your Profile:**


When you (or your friends) view your profile, here's what you see:


**1. Cover Photo and Profile Picture**

- At the top: Large banner (cover photo)
- Circular photo: Your profile picture
- These visually represent you

**2. Your Name and Basic Info**

- Your name
- Optional: Tagline or bio
- Location, work, school (if you added them)

**3. Navigation Menu (below your name):**

- **Posts** - Everything you've posted
- **About** - Your biographical information
- **Friends** - Your friends list
- **Photos** - All photos of you or that you've posted
- **Videos** - Videos you've shared
- **Check-ins** - Places you've visited (if you use this feature)
- **More** - Additional sections

**4. Your Timeline**

- Scrolling down, you see all your posts in reverse chronological order (newest first)
- Posts from years ago are further down
- This is your "history" on Facebook

**Understanding Your Timeline:**


Your timeline is the story of your time on Facebook.


**What appears on your timeline:**

- Posts you created
- Photos you posted or were tagged in
- Life events you added (moved, changed job, etc.)
- Comments from friends on your posts
- Things friends posted to your timeline (if you allow this)

**Timeline navigation:**

- Scroll down to see older posts
- On the right side (computer) or at the top (phone), you can select specific years
- Click a year to jump to posts from that time period

**Editing Your About Section:**


This is where you share information about yourself.

1. On your profile, click **"About"**
2. You'll see categories:
    - **Overview** - Summary of key info
    - **Work and Education** - Job history, schools attended
    - **Places You've Lived** - Current city, hometown
    - **Contact and Basic Info** - Birthday, phone, email, etc.
    - **Family and Relationships** - Relationship status, family members
    - **Details About You** - Hobbies, interests, favorite quotes
    - **Life Events** - Major milestones

**For each section:**

1. Click **"Edit"** or the pencil icon
2. Add or change information
3. Use the **privacy icon** next to each item to control who sees it
    - Set most things to **"Friends"** or **"Only me"**
4. Click **"Save"**

**What to include:**

- Current city (helpful for friends to see)
- Hometown (nostalgia, helps old friends find you)
- Schools attended (connects you with classmates)
- General work history (if comfortable sharing)

**What to keep private or skip:**

- Phone number (set to "Only me")
- Exact address (don't add this)
- Very personal details
- Anything that makes you uncomfortable

**Viewing Your Profile As Others See It:**


Want to see what your profile looks like to others?

1. On your profile, click the **three dots** next to "Edit Profile"
2. Click **"View As"**
3. Select:
    - **"View as Public"** - What strangers see
    - **"View as [Specific Friend]"** - What that friend sees
4. This shows you exactly what they can see
5. If you see information you don't want visible, go back and adjust privacy settings

**Featuring and Pinning Posts:**


You can highlight certain posts to appear prominently.


**Pinning a post** (keeps it at the top of your timeline):

1. Find a post you want to feature
2. Click the **three dots** on the post
3. Click **"Pin to top of profile"**
4. It stays at the top for 7 days

**Why you might pin:**

- Important announcement (graduation, new grandchild, etc.)
- Photo you're particularly proud of
- Information you want visitors to see first

**Organizing Your Timeline:**


**Life Events:**


You can add major milestones to your timeline.

1. On your profile, click **"Life Event"** (under cover photo or in the "What's on your mind?" box)
2. Choose a category:
    - Family & Relationships (marriage, birth, new pet)
    - Home & Living (moved, home improvement)
    - Work & Education (new job, retirement, graduation)
    - Health & Wellness (quit smoking, started exercising)
    - Travel & Experiences (traveled somewhere, memorable experience)
    - Interests & Activities (read a great book, learned a new skill)
3. Fill in details
4. Choose privacy setting
5. Choose date
6. Click **"Share"**

**Life events appear on your timeline with special formatting, marking important moments.**


**Archive vs. Delete:**


**Archive** - Hide posts without deleting them:

1. Click three dots on a post
2. Click **"Move to archive"**
3. The post is hidden from your timeline but saved
4. You can restore it later

**Delete** - Permanently remove:

1. Click three dots on post
2. Click **"Move to trash"**
3. Confirm deletion

**Why archive instead of delete:**

- Keeps memories but declutters timeline
- Can restore if you change your mind
- Good for old posts that no longer represent you
> **Your Profile is Your Story:** Think of your profile as a scrapbook of your life on Facebook. You control what goes in it, what stays visible, and how you present yourself. It's okay to curate it to show the version of yourself you're comfortable sharing.

## Step 9: Using Facebook Messenger (Private Messages)


Messenger is Facebook's private messaging system—like texting, but through Facebook. Let's learn how to send and receive messages.


**What is Facebook Messenger?**


Think of it like:

- Private letters vs. public bulletin board posts
- Text messages, but through Facebook instead of your phone carrier
- One-on-one or group conversations that only participants can see

**Messages vs. Posts:**

- **Posts** appear on timelines and News Feeds (your friends see them)
- **Messages** are private conversations (only the people you message see them)

**Accessing Messenger:**


**On a computer:**

- Click the **Messenger icon** (speech bubble with lightning bolt) in the top-right blue bar
- Or go to messenger.com in your browser

**On a smartphone:**

- You can use Messenger within the Facebook app
- Or download the separate **Messenger app** (Facebook recommends this)
    - Go to App Store or Play Store
    - Search "Messenger"
    - Download the blue app with a lightning bolt inside a speech bubble
    - Log in with your Facebook credentials

**Sending Your First Message:**


**On a computer:**

1. Click the **Messenger icon** at the top
2. Click **"New Message"** or the **pencil icon**
3. A message box opens
4. Type a friend's name in the "To:" field
5. Click their name when it appears
6. Type your message in the box at the bottom
7. Press **Enter** or click the **Send button** (paper airplane icon)

**On smartphone (Facebook app):**

1. Tap the **Messenger icon** at the top
2. Tap the **pencil/compose icon**
3. Type your friend's name
4. Select them from the list
5. Type your message
6. Tap the **Send arrow**

**What to message about:**


**Good reasons to message instead of posting:**

- Personal conversations
- Making plans ("Want to meet for lunch?")
- Sharing something meant just for that person
- Responding to something they posted privately
- Catching up without everyone seeing
- Sharing photos meant only for them
- Asking questions

**Example messages:**

- "Hi! Just wanted to say hello and see how you're doing."
- "Loved your post about the garden! Do you have any tips for growing tomatoes?"
- "Thank you for your kind comment on my photo!"
- "Would you like to get coffee sometime?"

**Reading Messages:**


When someone sends you a message:

1. You'll see a notification (red number) on the **Messenger icon**
2. Click or tap the Messenger icon
3. You'll see a list of conversations
4. Click or tap a conversation to open it
5. Read the messages
6. Type a reply at the bottom
7. Send

**Message Features:**


**Sending Photos:**

1. Open a conversation
2. Click the **photo icon** (camera or picture frame)
3. Select a photo from your computer or phone
4. It attaches to the message
5. Send

**Sending Emojis:**

1. Click the **smiley face icon**
2. A panel of emojis opens (😊 🎉 ❤️ 👍 etc.)
3. Click one to add it to your message
4. Send

**Voice Messages (phone only):**

1. Tap and hold the **microphone icon**
2. Speak your message
3. Release to send
4. The recipient can play the audio

**Video Chat:**

1. Open a conversation
2. Click or tap the **video camera icon** at the top
3. The call rings the other person
4. If they answer, you have a video call (like FaceTime or Skype)

**Managing Conversations:**


**Archiving conversations:**


If you want to hide a conversation without deleting it:


**On computer:**

1. Hover over the conversation in your list
2. Click the **three dots**
3. Click **"Archive"**
4. The conversation is hidden but saved

**On phone:**

1. Swipe left on the conversation (iPhone)
2. Tap **"Archive"**

**Deleting messages:**

1. In the conversation, hover over (computer) or hold down (phone) a specific message
2. Click **"Remove"** or **"Delete"**
3. Choose "Delete for everyone" (removes for both people) or "Delete for you" (only removes your copy)

**Blocking someone:**


If someone is bothering you in messages:

1. Open the conversation
2. Click their **name** at the top
3. Click **"Block"** (in their profile or settings)
4. They can no longer message you

**Message Requests:**


When someone who isn't your Facebook friend messages you, it goes to **Message Requests** instead of your main inbox.


**To check message requests:**

1. Open Messenger
2. Click or tap **"Message Requests"** (often in settings or at the top)
3. You'll see messages from non-friends
4. You can:
    - **Accept** - Moves conversation to main inbox and you can reply
    - **Delete** - Removes the message request

**Don't accept requests from:**

- People you don't know
- Suspicious profiles (new accounts, very few friends)
- People asking for money
- Anyone making you uncomfortable

**Messenger Safety:**


**Red flags in messages:**


❌ "I need money urgently" - Even if from a friend (their account might be hacked)
❌ Links you didn't expect - Could be phishing or viruses
❌ Messages claiming you won something
❌ Requests for passwords or personal information
❌ Strangers being overly friendly or romantic
❌ Anyone asking for gift cards or wire transfers


**Safe practices:**

- Only message people you know
- Don't click unexpected links
- If a friend sends a weird message, call them on the phone to verify
- Never send money to someone you've only talked to on Facebook
- Don't share passwords, bank info, or Social Security number

**Group Conversations:**


You can message multiple people at once.


**Creating a group message:**

1. Click **New Message**
2. Type multiple names in the "To:" field
3. Type your message
4. Everyone in the group sees all messages
5. Good for coordinating events or family discussions

**Naming a group:**

1. Open the group conversation
2. Click the **information icon** (i)
3. Click **"Change Name"**
4. Type a name like "Smith Family" or "Book Club"
> **Messenger Tips:** Think of Messenger as phone calls or letters—personal and private. Use posts for public updates everyone should see. Use messages for personal conversations. Most people use messages more than posts on Facebook.

## Step 10: Staying Safe on Facebook (Avoiding Scams and Problems)


Facebook is generally safe, but like any public place, you need to be aware of potential problems. Let's learn how to protect yourself.


**Common Facebook Scams to Watch For:**


**Scam #1: The Cloned Friend Account**


**What happens:**

- You receive a friend request from someone you're already friends with
- Their profile looks similar to their real one
- After you accept, they message asking for money or sharing a "great investment opportunity"

**The truth:** A scammer copied your friend's profile and photos to create a fake account.


**What to do:**

- Don't accept duplicate friend requests
- Message your real friend (on their original account or by phone) to let them know
- Report the fake account to Facebook

**Scam #2: "You Won!" Messages**


**What happens:**

- You get a message saying you won a prize, lottery, or grant money
- They ask you to pay fees, taxes, or shipping to claim it
- Or they ask for bank information

**The truth:** You didn't win anything. It's a scam to steal your money.


**What to do:**

- Delete the message
- Report the sender
- Remember: Real prizes never require upfront payment

**Scam #3: The "Is This You?" Link**


**What happens:**

- A friend sends you a message: "OMG is this you in this video??" with a link
- If you click the link, it takes you to a fake Facebook login page
- You enter your password thinking you need to log in
- Now scammers have your password

**The truth:** Your friend's account was hacked. The link steals passwords.


**What to do:**

- Don't click the link
- Call your friend on the phone to tell them they were hacked
- Never enter your password after clicking a link in a message

**Scam #4: Romance Scams**


**What happens:**

- An attractive stranger sends you a friend request
- They start chatting and quickly become very friendly or romantic
- Eventually, they have an "emergency" and need money
- They promise to pay you back or meet you in person
- After you send money, they disappear or create another emergency

**The truth:** They're professional scammers, often part of organized criminal networks.


**What to do:**

- Don't accept friend requests from strangers
- Never send money to someone you've only met online
- If someone you've never met in person asks for money, block them

**Scam #5: Fake Facebook Employee**


**What happens:**

- You get a message from "Facebook Security Team"
- They say your account will be deleted unless you verify your information
- They ask for your password or other personal details

**The truth:** Facebook never contacts users via message asking for passwords.


**What to do:**

- Ignore and delete
- Facebook will never ask for your password
- Real security issues appear when you log into Facebook, not via message

**How to Spot Fake Accounts and Profiles:**


**Red flags indicating a fake account:**


❌ **Profile picture is of a very attractive model-type person**

- Often stolen from the internet

❌ **Account was just created recently**

- Check when they joined Facebook (should show on profile)
- New accounts (this month or week) are suspicious

❌ **Very few friends (under 20)**

- Real people accumulate friends over time

❌ **Only one or two photos**

- Real profiles have multiple photos over time

❌ **No personal posts, just shares**

- Real people post about their actual lives

❌ **Profile information doesn't make sense**

- Says they're from Texas but all text is in poor English
- Photos of Asian person but name is "John Smith"

❌ **Lots of typos and grammatical errors**

- Many scammers operate from non-English-speaking countries

**Protecting Your Account:**


**Security Checklist:**


✓ **Strong, unique password** - Not used anywhere else
✓ **Enable two-factor authentication** - Sends code to your phone when logging in
✓ **Privacy settings set to "Friends"** - Posts only visible to friends
✓ **Profile information limited** - Don't share phone number or address publicly
✓ **Email and phone set to private** - Only you can see them
✓ **Review friend requests carefully** - Only accept people you know


**If You Think You Were Hacked:**


**Signs your account was hacked:**

- Friends tell you you're sending strange messages
- You see posts you didn't make
- Can't log in with your password
- You get password reset emails you didn't request

**Immediate actions:**

1. **Try to log in and change password immediately**
2. **If you can log in:**
    - Settings > Security and Login > Change Password
    - Log out all other sessions (Settings > Security and Login > Where You're Logged In > Log Out All Sessions)
    - Check recent posts and delete anything suspicious
3. **If you can't log in:**
    - Go to facebook.com/hacked
    - Follow the account recovery process
4. **After regaining access:**
    - Enable two-factor authentication
    - Change password on any other sites where you used the same password
    - Warn friends your account was compromised

**Reporting Problems to Facebook:**


**To report a profile, post, or message:**

1. Click the **three dots** on the post, profile, or message
2. Click **"Report"** or **"Find Support or Report Post"**
3. Choose the reason:
    - Scam or fraud
    - Fake account
    - Harassment
    - Hate speech
    - Spam
4. Follow the prompts
5. Facebook will review (may take days to weeks)

**What NOT to Share on Facebook:**


For your safety and privacy:


❌ **Home address** - Tells strangers where you live
❌ **Phone number** - Leads to spam calls and scams
❌ **Vacation plans in real-time** - "We're in Hawaii for 2 weeks!" tells burglars your home is empty
❌ **Financial information** - Credit card numbers, bank account info
❌ **Social Security number** - Even partial numbers
❌ **Photos of credit cards or IDs** - Can be used for identity theft
❌ **Passwords or security question answers** - Those "Your first car + street name = your superhero name" posts collect security question answers
❌ **Daily schedule** - "Every Tuesday at 10 AM I go to the gym" tells people when you're not home
❌ **Boarding passes or tickets** - Contain personal information that can be stolen


**Recognizing Misinformation:**


Not everything on Facebook is true. Be skeptical of:


**Warning signs of false information:**

- Shocking or too-good-to-be-true headlines
- Claims with no source cited
- Posts claiming "Share this before Facebook deletes it!"
- Miracle cures or get-rich-quick schemes
- Posts that make you very angry or scared (designed to manipulate emotions)
- "Copy and paste" posts (usually chain letters)

**Before sharing, ask:**

- Is this from a reputable news source?
- Have I verified this with another source?
- Does this seem designed to make me emotional so I'll share it?
- Would I be embarrassed if this turns out to be false?

**Fact-checking resources:**

- Snopes.com
- FactCheck.org
- Major news outlets (AP News, Reuters, BBC, NPR)

**When in doubt, don't share it.**

> **Trust Your Instincts:** If something feels wrong—a message, a friend request, a post asking you to do something—it probably is wrong. Your intuition is usually right. When in doubt, don't click, don't send money, don't share personal information. Ask a trusted friend or family member first.

## Step 11: Understanding the News Feed and What You See


Your News Feed is the main page of Facebook—but what determines what you see? Let's understand how it works and how to control it.


**What is the News Feed Algorithm?**


Think of the algorithm like a newspaper editor from the 1960s who decides which articles go on the front page. Facebook's algorithm decides which posts appear at the top of your feed based on what it thinks you'll be most interested in.


**What affects what you see:**

1. **Posts you interact with** - If you like, comment, or share posts about gardening, you'll see more gardening content
2. **Recent posts** - Newer posts generally appear higher
3. **Popular posts** - Posts with lots of engagement (likes, comments) may appear higher
4. **Friends you interact with most** - You'll see more from friends you frequently engage with
5. **Groups and Pages you follow** - Their content appears in your feed
6. **Ads** - Facebook inserts advertisements throughout your feed

**Your feed is NOT chronological.** Facebook doesn't show every post from every friend in time order. It picks and chooses what to show you.


**Why You Might Miss Posts:**


**Common reasons:**

- Facebook's algorithm didn't prioritize it
- You don't interact much with that friend
- The post was made when you weren't on Facebook
- It was buried under more "popular" content

**Solution:** If you want to see everything from a specific friend, you can adjust settings (we'll cover this below).


**Controlling What You See:**


**Option 1: See Posts from Specific Friends First**


**To prioritize a friend's posts:**

1. Go to that friend's profile
2. Click **"Following"** or **"Friends"** button
3. Select **"Favorites"** or **"See First"**
4. Their posts will now appear at the top of your feed

**Good for:**

- Close family members
- Best friends
- People whose posts you don't want to miss

**Option 2: Hide Posts You Don't Want to See**


If someone posts things you don't enjoy:

1. Click the **three dots** on one of their posts
2. Choose:
    - **"Hide post"** - Removes this specific post
    - **"Snooze [Friend Name] for 30 days"** - Temporarily stops seeing their posts (they won't know)
    - **"Unfollow [Friend Name]"** - Permanently stop seeing their posts but stay friends

**Why unfollow instead of unfriend:**

- You remain friends (they can still see your posts)
- You just don't see their posts in your feed
- Good for people who post too much or post things that upset you
- They're not notified that you unfollowed

**Option 3: Hide Topics You Don't Want to See**


Facebook can reduce certain topics:

1. When you see a post about a topic you don't want (politics, sports, certain news):
    - Click the three dots
    - Select **"Hide post"**
    - Select **"See fewer posts like this"**
2. Facebook learns your preferences over time

**Understanding Sponsored Posts (Ads):**


As you scroll, you'll see posts labeled **"Sponsored"** or **"Suggested for you"**.


**What these are:**

- Advertisements from businesses
- Posts from pages you don't follow
- Facebook's way of making money (the service is free because of ads)

**They're mixed in with regular posts but clearly labeled.**


**Controlling ads:**


You can't eliminate ads, but you can hide ones you don't like:

1. Click the **three dots** on the ad
2. Click **"Hide ad"**
3. Optionally tell Facebook why (seeing too often, not relevant, etc.)

**Over time, ads become more relevant to your interests.**


**Sorting Your News Feed:**


**Switch between feed types:**


**On computer:**

- Look in the left sidebar
- Click **"News Feed"** or **"Home"**
- You might see options like:
    - **Most Recent** - Chronological order (newest first)
    - **Favorites** - Only from friends you marked as favorites
    - **Following** - Only from pages and groups you follow

**On smartphone:**

- At the top of your feed, look for filter options
- Tap to switch between **"Home"** (algorithm) and **"Favorites"** (chronological from favorite friends)

**"On This Day" - Facebook Memories:**


Facebook shows you posts from the same date in previous years.


**Finding Memories:**

1. Look in the left sidebar (computer) or Menu (phone)
2. Click **"Memories"**
3. You'll see posts from this day in past years

**This is a fun way to:**

- Reminisce about the past
- See how you or your friends have changed
- Reshare old photos with new comments

**You can turn off memories if they make you sad (past losses, difficult times):**

1. Go to Memories
2. Settings (gear icon)
3. Adjust notification settings or hide specific people/dates

**Why Your Feed Feels Overwhelming:**


**Common complaints:**

- "Too much political content"
- "I see the same people over and over"
- "I miss posts from close friends"
- "Too many ads and suggested content"

**Solutions:**

- Unfollow people who post things you don't enjoy (stay friends, just don't see their posts)
- Mark close friends as "Favorites" so you always see their posts
- Hide or snooze topics you don't want
- Take breaks from Facebook when it feels overwhelming
- Remember: You control your experience—curate it to be positive
> **Your Feed, Your Rules:** Facebook gives you significant control over what you see. Use the "Hide," "Snooze," and "Unfollow" options liberally. Facebook is supposed to make you feel connected and happy. If it's doing the opposite, adjust what you see until it feels positive again.

## Step 12: Facebook Groups, Pages, and Events


Beyond connecting with friends, Facebook offers ways to join communities and follow organizations. Let's explore these features.


**Facebook Groups - Joining Communities:**


**What are Groups?**


Groups are like clubs on Facebook. They're collections of people interested in the same topic, hobby, or location.


**Examples:**

- "Rochester NY Community"
- "Quilting and Sewing Enthusiasts"
- "Classic Car Restoration"
- "Book Lovers Book Club"
- "[Your High School] Class of 1965"
- "Grandparents Raising Grandchildren Support"

**Types of groups:**


**Public Groups:**

- Anyone can find them
- Anyone can see posts
- Anyone can join

**Private Groups:**

- Anyone can find the group, but can't see posts unless they're a member
- Must request to join or be invited

**Secret Groups (now called "Hidden Groups"):**

- Can't be found in search
- Only members can see the group exists
- Must be invited by a current member

**Finding and Joining Groups:**


**Method 1: Search**

1. Click the **search bar** at the top
2. Type what you're interested in: "knitting" or "gardening" or "Rochester NY"
3. Click **"Groups"** in the left filter menu
4. Browse groups related to your search
5. Click on a group to preview it
6. Click **"Join Group"** or **"Request to Join"**
7. For private groups, an admin must approve your request (may take hours or days)

**Method 2: Recommendations**

1. Click **"Groups"** in the left menu (computer) or Menu tab (phone)
2. Scroll to **"Suggested For You"**
3. Facebook shows groups based on your interests and friends' groups
4. Click any that interest you
5. Join

**Method 3: Friends' Groups**


If you see a friend post in a group:

1. Click on the group name in their post
2. Preview the group
3. Join if interested

**Participating in Groups:**


**Viewing group posts:**

1. Click **"Groups"** in the menu
2. Click the group name
3. You'll see posts from group members (like a News Feed but only for that group)

**Posting in a group:**

1. In the group, find the **"Write something..."** box
2. Type your post
3. Click **"Post"**
4. All group members can see it

**Why join groups:**

- Connect with people who share your interests
- Get advice or recommendations
- Learn new things
- Feel part of a community
- Buy/sell locally (marketplace groups)
- Coordinate activities or events

**Group etiquette:**

- Read the group rules (usually pinned at the top)
- Be respectful and kind
- Stay on topic
- Don't spam or advertise (unless it's a selling group)
- Search before asking common questions

**Leaving a group:**

1. Go to the group
2. Click **"Joined"** or the three dots
3. Click **"Leave Group"**
4. Confirm

**Facebook Pages - Following Organizations:**


**What are Pages?**


Pages are like official accounts for:

- Businesses (local restaurants, stores)
- Public figures (politicians, celebrities)
- Organizations (charities, churches, schools)
- Media (newspapers, TV stations)
- Brands (Coca-Cola, Ford, etc.)

**Pages vs. Profiles:**

- **Profiles** are for individual people
- **Pages** are for organizations, businesses, and public figures
- You "friend" profiles but "like" or "follow" pages
- Pages can have unlimited followers

**Finding and Following Pages:**


**Method 1: Search**

1. Search for a business, organization, or person
2. Click **"Pages"** in the left filter
3. Click on the page
4. Click **"Like"** or **"Follow"** (or both)

**Difference between Like and Follow:**

- **Like** - Shows you support the page
- **Follow** - You'll see their posts in your News Feed
- Usually you want to do both

**Method 2: Recommendations**


Facebook suggests pages based on:

- Your interests
- Pages your friends like
- Your location

**To see suggestions:**

1. Look in your News Feed for "Suggested Pages"
2. Or go to Menu > **"Pages"** > **"Discover"**

**Examples of useful pages to follow:**


**Local:**

- Your town/city page
- Local library
- Local news station
- Favorite local restaurants

**Organizations:**

- Your church or place of worship
- Charities you support
- Alumni associations
- Veterans groups

**Interests:**

- National Geographic
- Cooking shows you enjoy
- Authors you like
- Museums or cultural institutions

**News:**

- Newspapers you trust
- News channels
- Weather services

**Interacting with pages:**


You can like, comment, and share page posts just like friends' posts.


**Pages you follow will:**

- Appear in your News Feed
- Send you notifications (if you allow)
- See your public information when you interact

**Unfollowing or Unliking pages:**

1. Go to the page
2. Click **"Following"** or **"Liked"**
3. Select **"Unfollow"** or **"Unlike"**

**Facebook Events:**


**What are Events?**


Events are digital invitations for:

- Parties and celebrations
- Community gatherings
- Classes or workshops
- Fundraisers
- Reunions
- Online events (webinars, live streams)

**Finding Events:**


**Method 1: Invitations**


When someone invites you to an event:

1. You'll get a notification
2. Click on it
3. You'll see event details:
    - Date and time
    - Location (or "online event")
    - Description
    - Who else is going
4. Respond:
    - **Going** - You plan to attend
    - **Interested** - Maybe going, want updates
    - **Can't Go** - Decline

**Method 2: Local Events**

1. Click **"Events"** in the left menu (computer) or Menu (phone)
2. Browse local events happening near you
3. Filter by:
    - Today, Tomorrow, This Week, etc.
    - Categories (Music, Food & Drink, Sports, etc.)

**Creating an Event:**


You can create events for parties, gatherings, or meetups:

1. Click **"Events"** in menu
2. Click **"Create Event"** or the plus sign
3. Choose:
    - **In Person** - Physical location
    - **Online** - Virtual event
4. Fill in:
    - Event name: "Sarah's 70th Birthday Party"
    - Date and time
    - Location (address or link)
    - Description: What the event is about
    - Privacy: Public (anyone), Friends, or Invite Only
5. Click **"Create"**
6. Invite friends by selecting them from your list
7. Click **"Post"**

**Event notifications:**


Events you're interested in or going to will:

- Appear in your Events list
- Send you reminders as the date approaches
- Show updates if the host posts

**Benefits of groups, pages, and events:**

- Connect with communities beyond your friend list
- Stay informed about local happenings
- Learn from experts and enthusiasts
- Coordinate gatherings easily
- Discover new interests
> **Start Slow:** You don't need to join dozens of groups or follow hundreds of pages right away. Start with 2-3 groups about interests you're passionate about, follow local businesses and organizations you care about, and see how it feels. You can always add more later.

## Common Questions Answered


**"How much time should I spend on Facebook?"**


There's no right answer—it depends on what makes you happy. Some people check once a day for 10 minutes. Others enjoy scrolling for an hour. Just be aware if it's:

- Interfering with real-life relationships or activities
- Making you feel anxious or bad about yourself
- Becoming a compulsive habit

If any of these are true, consider reducing your time or taking breaks.


**"Do I have to post things? Can I just read what others post?"**


Absolutely! Many people "lurk" (read without posting) and that's completely fine. Facebook is valuable even if you never post—you can still stay connected by seeing friends' updates and liking/commenting on them.


**"What if I make a mistake or post something embarrassing?"**


You can edit or delete any post you make. Click the three dots on your post and select "Edit" or "Delete." Everyone makes mistakes on Facebook—don't worry about it. Just fix it and move on.


**"How do I know if someone read my post?"**


You can see who liked or commented, but you can't see who simply viewed it without interacting (unlike on some other platforms). This is by design for privacy.


**"Can I use Facebook without a smartphone?"**


Yes! Facebook works perfectly fine on computers and tablets. You don't need a smartphone, though the mobile app does offer some convenience.


**"What's the difference between Facebook and Instagram/Twitter/TikTok?"**

- **Facebook**: All-purpose social network, focuses on connections with people you know, longer posts, diverse content
- **Instagram**: Photo and video focused, younger demographic, more visual
- **Twitter**: Short text posts, news and current events focused
- **TikTok**: Short videos, entertainment focused, very young demographic

Facebook is generally the best starting point for older adults connecting with family and friends.


**"My grandkids use Instagram—should I get that instead?"**


You can use both! But Facebook tends to have more users in your age group, making it easier to connect with friends and family your age. Your grandkids might also have Facebook accounts even if they prefer Instagram.


**"How do I stop seeing political posts?"**


Use the Hide, Snooze, and Unfollow features liberally. You can also join groups and follow pages focused on hobbies and interests rather than news, which shifts your feed toward more positive content.


**"Someone is harassing me—what do I do?"**


Block them immediately (go to their profile > three dots > Block). Report them to Facebook if they're violating rules. You can also unfriend them and adjust your privacy settings. You're never obligated to accept friend requests or interact with anyone who makes you uncomfortable.


**"Is Facebook listening to my conversations through my phone?"**


This is a common concern. Facebook and Meta claim they don't listen through your microphone. However, they do track your browsing on other websites and apps, which is why ads seem eerily relevant. You can limit this tracking in your phone's privacy settings.


**"Can Facebook access my photos without permission?"**


Facebook can only access photos you explicitly upload or share. They can't randomly browse your device. However, when you upload photos, Facebook does use them according to their terms of service (including for facial recognition unless you opt out).


**"What happens to my account if I die?"**


You can designate a "legacy contact" who can manage your account after your death, or request that Facebook delete it. Go to Settings > Memorialization Settings to set this up. Otherwise, your account can be "memorialized" (frozen as a memorial) if someone notifies Facebook of your death.


**"I'm overwhelmed—is there a simpler way to use Facebook?"**


Absolutely. Focus only on:

- Viewing your News Feed
- Liking friends' posts
- Posting occasionally (once a week or less)
- Messaging close friends

Ignore everything else—stories, marketplace, groups, games, etc. Use only the features that make sense to you. Facebook has too many features for anyone to use them all.


## You're Now Ready to Use Facebook!


Congratulations on making it through this guide! You now know:

- How to create and set up a Facebook account
- How to adjust privacy settings for safety
- How to add a profile picture and find friends
- How to create posts and interact with others' posts
- How to send private messages
- How to navigate your profile and News Feed
- How to stay safe from scams
- How to use groups, pages, and events
- How to control what you see and customize your experience

**Your Action Plan:**


**Week 1:**

- Create your account if you haven't
- Set privacy settings
- Add profile picture
- Find and add 5-10 close friends and family

**Week 2:**

- Make your first post
- Practice liking and commenting on friends' posts
- Send a message to someone
- Explore your News Feed

**Week 3:**

- Join 1-2 groups about your interests
- Follow a few local businesses or organizations
- Adjust what you see based on your preferences
- Get comfortable with daily browsing

**Week 4 and beyond:**

- Use Facebook at your own pace
- Add more friends gradually
- Post when you have something to share
- Stay safe by following the security guidelines

**Remember:**


**Take your time.** You don't need to master everything immediately. Facebook has been around since 2004 and will continue to be here—there's no rush.


**Use what works for you.** Not every feature will appeal to you, and that's fine. Create your own Facebook experience based on what brings you joy.


**Ask for help.** If you get stuck, ask a tech-savvy friend or family member. Most people are happy to help, and you can also search YouTube for "how to [whatever you're trying to do] on Facebook."


**Stay safe.** Follow the security guidelines in this guide. Be cautious about friend requests from strangers and never send money to people you've only met online.


**Be yourself.** Facebook is most rewarding when you're authentic. Share what genuinely interests you, connect with people you truly care about, and don't feel pressure to perform or present a perfect image.


**Most importantly:** Facebook is a tool to enhance your life—to stay connected with loved ones, share joyful moments, and participate in communities. If it's doing that for you, wonderful. If it ever stops serving that purpose, it's okay to take a break or use it less. You're in control.


Welcome to Facebook—enjoy staying connected with the people you care about!
